<!-- pr-reviewer: 0754f88cf31bc485a333169e3b3f0a56604e5172 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This is a careful, well-argued piece of work. The safety design holds up under probing. There are two things to fix: the land model does nothing for Pencil and Corner, yet their path still gets the "flown over" note, and the new file key has no round-trip test.

### What looks good
- The safety argument is structural. The lids live only in a local `drive` slice inside the Finish3D arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:855`). Verify, the rest material, stock sim and every other consumer still read `material.facets`, so nothing downstream can see a lid.
- `fill.rs` re-asserts `closed >= H`. Lids never sit above the local maximum height, and the model facets come first and stay unchanged. Probes over 12 patterns found no extra bite into the real model with the fill on (numbers below).
- The closure rule is conservative. Openings that touch the edge (a blind notch, a through notch), a hole on a staircase with a lower rim, and a large pocket at a coarse grid all fall back to "not filled". None of them is filled wrongly.
- Geodesic + fill is refused by name. 3D Finish is already ball-only, so a flat or bull cutter never reaches the fill.
- Width validation runs at command creation (`sane.rs`), at the generator (`fill.rs:72`) and over MCP (0 is refused). Undo works through `EditOperationParams` and is pinned over MCP.
- When the option is off, nothing changes byte for byte: no file key and no digest bytes. `golden_cl` passes and no file under `tests/golden/` changed.
- The provenance names public literature (Serra 1982, Soille 2003). The new file is 326 lines, with no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Degenerate input is refused by name (non-finite facets, an empty model, a too-fine width, a 1e9 mm model). No snapshot PNGs changed and no process files were touched.

### Local results (trial-merged with `origin/main` 53a52f88, merged cleanly)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` | 202 passed, 1 ignored |
| motion `finish3d_land` | 4 passed (1.2 s) |
| app `area_controls` | 13 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `operations` | 118 passed, 6 ignored (33 s) |
| app `mcp` | 19 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (cwd `crates/ui`) | 616 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

`motion:finish3d` was not run. It is in the slow list, and no existing generator changed.

**Throwaway probes (local only, never pushed).** Each probe ran a 3 mm ball on a 40x20x8 plate with fill on and off. Two measures were taken: the lowest feed Z over each opening, and the deepest ball bite measured against the **real** model. The bite was taken at feed tips; the dense chord sampling also matches between on and off, and its only hits are arc chords.
- Through hole + blind pocket, w = 5: 2 openings were lidded. Parallel, radial, spiral, contour, blend and morphed spiral stay at Z 8.000 over both openings (off: the path falls through the hole and to Z 4.0 in the pocket). Waterline and morph do not enter. The bite on the real model is 0.009 for both on and off, and a path sunk 0.5 mm reads a 0.58 bite.
- Pocket (floor 2) with a 2 mm boss at 6, 8 and 10 mm, w = 10: 1 opening each time. Over the gap the path holds Z 8 (off: Z 2). Over the boss it holds Z 8, or Z 10 where the boss stands proud, so the lid never sits under real material. The bite matches the off run.
- An opening cut by the boundary (a blind notch and a through notch open at y = 0): 0 openings, and the path matches the off run.
- Nested openings (pocket floor 4 with a through hole, w = 3 and w = 14): w = 3 lids only the inner hole, at Z 4. w = 14 lids the whole pocket, at Z 8.
- Large pocket (36x16 with a 2 mm rim, w = 50): 0 openings, because the cell is 4.2 mm and misses the rim. This is safe (nothing is filled) but worth knowing (note 2).
- Runtime: a 300x300 plate at w = 3.5 fills in 3.7 s in debug. A half shell plus zero-area facets gives no panic and 0 openings.

### Requested before merge
1. **Pencil and Corner ignore the lids, yet they get the land note.** See `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:876-877` and `:935-937`. `pencil`/`corner` walk crease loci from the mesh's shared-edge index (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/pencil.rs:113-117`), and the lids share no edges with the model. So the creases inside a lidded opening are still found and cut under the lid. In the probes, with fill on, Pencil and Corner went to Z 4.318 in the lidded blind pocket, Z 2.0 in the lidded boss pocket and Z -0.045 in the lidded through hole. Those are exactly the same moves as with fill off. Meanwhile the path says `land: N closed opening(s) ... filled at their rim and flown over, not cut`. This is not a gouge (the bite on the real model is 0), but the path note states the opposite of what the path does, on an op under the safety floor. The PR body's claim that every finishing law keeps the ball off every facet it is given does not hold for these two in the way the fill needs. Fix: refuse `Pencil`/`Corner` with `fill_openings` by name, as Geodesic is (for example, "Pencil cleans the creases inside openings, so it cannot fill them - clear 'Fill openings' or pick another pattern"), and add a test. Making pencil honour the lids is the alternative. Please also confirm Flow (`multiaxis::flow3d`), which I did not probe.
2. **Round-trip test for the new file key.** `ParamsDto::Finish3D.fill_openings` (`crates/app/src/project/params.rs:499-503`, `params_impl.rs:388/1570`) has no `project_roundtrip` test. Add one that saves and loads an op with `Some(5.0)` and gets `Some(5.0)` back, and one that shows an older file without the key reads `None`. It is a small test, and it is what keeps the optional key from being dropped silently in a later refactor.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The note is pushed even when nothing was filled (`land: 0 closed opening(s) ...`). Consider saying "no closed opening narrower than W mm found - the path follows the model" in that case.
2. The grid follows the width (cell = w/12). A large width therefore misses thin rims: in the large-pocket probe, a 2 mm rim was not sampled and nothing was filled. This is safe, but the decision file's line "filling every closed depression ... available by stating a large width" is not quite true. Consider clamping the cell by the finish tolerance or the tool radius, or reword that line.
3. The emptiness test samples cell centres, and lids are emitted per row at each cell's closed height. A large cap over a curved floor can therefore produce many lid triangles (2 per run), which every generator then scans. It was fine in the probes; it is worth watching on the reporter's STEP part.
4. Runtime is bounded by the 4M-cell cap. It took about 3.7 s in debug at about 2.6M cells, and the run is not cancellable. That is acceptable for an opt-in.
5. `generate.rs` was already over the ~400-line guide (3302 to 3322 lines). The growth is small; this is flagged only.
6. UI hint (`mill3d_page.rs:262`): "their walls stand as land; the verdict still judges the real model" reads a little like project jargon. "The walls stay uncut; the gouge check still uses the real model" may read more plainly.
7. A hole on a sloped face whose lower rim drops more than about one cell is not filled (by design: the rim check). The path note could say so, but this is not required.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 437f15354e5403dbf9e0170e6ebcb7b3b02a1d68 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so at the next cut). Both changes requested in the 0754f88 review are answered, and the two new commits are small and correct.

### Earlier findings
1. **Pencil/Corner with the fill** - answered. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:846-858` now refuses both by name before any fill or path is made, so no land note can sit on a crease path. Pinned by `operations::finish3d_fill_openings_refuses_pencil_and_corner_by_name` (checks the pattern name, "cannot fill them", "Fill openings", and status stays `Never`). Flow is not refused; `finish3d_land::flow_honours_the_lids_and_never_descends_into_a_lidded_pocket` shows with the 8 mm pocket that flow reaches the floor with the fill off and stays above top-1 mm with it on, and the real-model bite is within tolerance. That settles my open question on Flow.
2. **Round-trip of the new file key** - answered. `project_roundtrip` `finish3d_fill_openings_round_trips_through_save_and_load` and `finish3d_file_without_fill_openings_reads_none` both pass.
3. Notes 1, 2 and 6 were applied (`fill.rs:62` says so when nothing is filled; decision file reworded; UI hint plainer). Notes 3, 4, 5, 7 were watch items.

### Local results (trial-merged with current `origin/main`, merged cleanly)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| motion `finish3d_land` | 6 passed |
| app `operations` | 119 passed, 6 ignored |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 73 passed |
| app `area_controls` | 13 passed |
| app `mcp` | 19 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (cwd `crates/ui`) | 628 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: `golden_cl` and the slow `finish3d` lane (the delta touches no generator when the option is off). Law check: no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` added outside tests, the refusal is by name, no process files, snapshot PNGs, `tests/golden/`, `CHANGELOG.md` or dependencies changed; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1196`.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. The refusal happens at generation, not at command creation (the same place Geodesic is refused). Validating it in `sane.rs` would show it before the op is ever generated; fine as is, matching Geodesic.
2. tbrasselle's comment (a non-collaborator, so it carries no marker weight) reports on the reporter's real part that the Parallel raster fragments around the lids (plunges 58 -> 294 with the fill on, each costing a retract-rapid-plunge) and that the roof's shallow V-crease is lidded as an "opening" (lifting the path 0.04-0.29 mm). Neither is a safety problem (the path only rises, and the verifier reads the real model), and mkinney's note says they are out of this round. I did not reproduce them (no STEP part). Since they decide whether the option is usable on #1196's actual part, the maintainer may want a follow-up issue filed before the cut, or a look first.
3. `generate.rs` remains over the ~400-line guide (flag only).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
